Copy triageSets and the awarenessEpisode keys into the E5 shells (P7-Y1, P7-Y2). Ids chosen here (nothing pinned them): episode e5_signin_pages, defend set e5_links_inbox, check forms general_form_a and general_form_b.

triageSets._prefix: Prefix for the full episode (id e5_signin_pages). The defend-only shell (id e5_signin_pages_defend) sets episode_e5_signin_pages_defend_defend_ instead, as E1 does. No stage on purpose, as in E1.
triageSets.title: Quayholt sign-in pages
triageSets.brief: Five pages are open in your browser, each one reached from a link in your Quayholt inbox this morning. For each one, choose Trust (you'd sign in), Report or Delete (you'd close it), then tick what you noticed. Press the address bar, the padlock and the certificate to look closer. Reporting a real page never costs you anything.

messages._worked: E5's worked item, in the shape of 11 section 4.2. F = 2. Report + both = 100, Report + lookalike only = 80, Delete + both = 70, Trust + none = 0.
messages.subject: From an email: 'Your session has expired'
messages.body: Your session has expired for security reasons. Sign in again to carry on. This is a secure page: look for the padlock in your address bar.

perFlagNote.lookalike_domain: Quayholt's sign-in page is sso.quayholt.example. This is quayholt-sso.example, a different site with the words joined by a hyphen, which is also why your password manager offered nothing
perFlagNote.padlock_myth: The padlock and the certificate are real, but they were issued to quayholt-sso.example. They show the connection is private to whoever runs that site, not that the site is Quayholt's

truth.ifTrusted: Your Quayholt email address and password would go to whoever runs quayholt-sso.example, who could then sign in as you and read your mail.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. That isn't our sign-in page. We've blocked quayholt-sso.example and pulled the email that linked to it from everyone's inbox.

messages._note: The real page the first item imitates, straight after it, so a learner who missed the first sees the safe version next (11 section 4.3).
messages.subject: From your bookmark: Quayholt sign-in
messages.body: Sign in with your Quayholt account.

whyFine.lookalike_domain: The address ends in quayholt.example, Quayholt's own domain. The 'sso.' in front is one of Quayholt's own services, just as 'hr.' or 'mail.' would be.
whyFine.padlock_myth: It has a padlock, as almost every site does. The reason to trust it is the address, not the padlock.
whyFine.default: You opened it from your own bookmark, the address is Quayholt's, and your password manager filled it in because it recognised the site.

messages.subject: From an email: 'Gordon McLeish shared a calendar with you'
messages.body: Gordon McLeish has shared the calendar 'Claims team rota' with you. Sign in to view it.

perFlagNote.lookalike_domain: Read the address slowly: quayho1t has a digit 1 where the l should be. 'calendar.' in front makes it look like one of Quayholt's own services, but the site is quayho1t.example, and your password manager stayed quiet for the same reason

truth.ifTrusted: Your password would go to whoever runs quayho1t.example. Gordon never shared a calendar.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Gordon didn't send that invitation, and quayho1t.example isn't ours. We've blocked it.

messages.subject: From an email: 'Your mailbox is 98% full'
messages.body: Your mailbox is almost full, and new email will be turned away from 5pm today. Sign in below to keep your mail. Our phone lines are very busy, so please use this page rather than ringing the service desk.

perFlagNote.lookalike_domain: The IT service desk is on servicedesk.quayholt.example. quayholt-support.example adds a word with a hyphen, so it's someone else's site, and your password manager didn't fill it in
perFlagNote.secrecy_or_bypass: 'Please use this page rather than ringing the service desk' steers you away from the one check that would show this up

truth.ifTrusted: Your password would go to whoever runs quayholt-support.example. Your mailbox was never full.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Your mailbox is fine, and that page isn't ours. We've blocked it, and we're helping anyone who signed in to change their password.

messages._note: The genuine IT page (11 section 3.2, E5). It asks for a password and gives a deadline, so 'it wants my password' is not on its own the tell.
messages.subject: From the intranet: Change your password
messages.body: Your password expires in 5 days. Choose a new one below. The service desk will never ask for your password by email or over the phone.

page.heading: Quayholt IT Service Desk: change your password

whyFine.lookalike_domain: servicedesk.quayholt.example ends in quayholt.example, Quayholt's own domain.
whyFine.secrecy_or_bypass: It points you towards the service desk, not away from it.
whyFine.default: You reached it from the intranet, the address is Quayholt's, your password manager filled in your current password, and five days' notice is the usual reminder, not a rush.

triageSets.title: Inbox and sign-in check
triageSets.brief: Ten items from a Quayholt Insurance inbox: emails, and pages opened from links. For each one, choose Trust, Report or Delete, then tick what you noticed. You'll see how you did at the end. Reporting a real message never costs you anything.

messages.subject: Third-floor kitchen closed on Thursday
messages.body:
Morning all,
The third-floor kitchen will be closed all day Thursday while the sink is replaced. The second-floor kitchen is open as normal.
Sorry for the shuffle.
Owen
Facilities

whyFine.default: Facilities' real address, a building notice, and nothing to click, pay or sign in to.

messages.subject: From an email: 'Benefits window closes Friday'
messages.body: Choose your benefits for next year before Friday, or your current choices will lapse. This is a secure page: check for the padlock, then sign in with your Quayholt account.

perFlagNote.lookalike_domain: Quayholt's benefits site is benefits.quayholt.example; this is quayholt-benefits.example, a different site with a hyphen, and your password manager offered nothing
perFlagNote.padlock_myth: The page tells you to check for the padlock, but the padlock was issued to quayholt-benefits.example. It shows the connection is private, not who you're talking to

truth.ifTrusted: Your Quayholt password would go to whoever runs quayholt-benefits.example.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. That isn't our benefits site, and nothing lapses on Friday. We've blocked it.

messages.subject: From the intranet: Staff benefits
messages.body: Sign in to see your benefits and make changes for next year.

whyFine.lookalike_domain: benefits.quayholt.example ends in quayholt.example, Quayholt's own domain.
whyFine.default: You came from the intranet, the address is Quayholt's, and your password manager recognised the site and filled it in.

messages.subject: Quick favour, are you in?
messages.body:
Are you at your desk? I'm on a site visit and locked out of my laptop. Could you send me your Quayholt sign-in so I can pull the claims report before 4? Keep it between us; going through IT will take all day.
Gordon

perFlagNote.senderTrust: Gordon's name on a personal inbox at inboxly.example, not quayholt.example
perFlagNote.secrecy_or_bypass: 'Keep it between us' and 'going through IT will take all day' ask you to skip the people who could help him properly
perFlagNote.urgencyCalibrated: 'Before 4' leaves no time to ring him and check

truth.ifTrusted: Whoever wrote it could sign in as you, read your mail and send messages in your name.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Gordon has his laptop and didn't send this. Nobody at Quayholt will ever ask for your password.

messages.subject: Next year's leave is now on the HR portal
messages.body:
Hi all,
Next year's annual leave allowance is now showing on the HR portal, so you can start booking.
{{link:leave}}
You can also reach it from the intranet home page.
Sofia
HR

whyFine.linkCredible: The link goes where it says, to the HR portal on Quayholt's own domain, and you could reach it from the intranet instead.
whyFine.default: HR's real address, a routine notice, and no hurry.

messages.subject: Payroll record check
messages.body:
Hi,
We're moving to a new payroll system and a few records don't match. Could you reply with your staff number and your home postcode so I can fix yours before the next run?
Thanks,
Pauline
Payroll

perFlagNote.senderAuth: SPF and DMARC both failed for quayholt.example: Quayholt's own servers didn't send this
perFlagNote.reply_to_differs: Replies go to p.hendry.payroll@inboxly.example, not to Pauline's Quayholt address

truth.headerNote: Open the details: the From shows Pauline's real address, but the checks failed and the reply-to points somewhere else.
truth.ifTrusted: Your staff number and postcode are what a caller needs to sound like you when they ring the service desk to reset your password.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Pauline didn't send it, and payroll isn't changing systems.

messages.subject: Back at your desk: the expenses tab you left open
messages.body: Your session timed out after 30 minutes without activity. Sign in again to carry on with your claim.

whyFine.lookalike_domain: expenses.quayholt.example ends in quayholt.example, Quayholt's own domain.
whyFine.default: A timed-out session is normal when a tab is left open. You opened this one yourself, the address is Quayholt's, and your password manager filled it in.

messages.subject: Ashcombe Solicitors shared 'Settlement papers' with you

perFlagNote.linkCredible: The link text says ashcombelaw.example, but it goes to docshare-login.example
perFlagNote.pretextRelevant: You have no case with Ashcombe, and legal papers reach Quayholt through the claims system, not a share link

truth.ifTrusted: The link opens a sign-in page that collects your Quayholt password.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Nobody here has a matter with Ashcombe, and the link went to a sign-in page we've now blocked.

messages.subject: Staff survey: ten minutes, anonymous
messages.body:
Hello,
This year's staff survey is open until the end of the month. It takes about ten minutes and doesn't ask you to sign in.
{{link:survey}}
Thank you,
The People Team

whyFine.senderAuth: SPF failed because the survey service sent it for Quayholt, but DKIM passed and DMARC passed for quayholt.example, the real domain.
whyFine.linkCredible: The link goes where it says, to Quayholt's own survey address, and the survey asks for no sign-in.
whyFine.default: The People Team's real address, a survey with a month to answer, and nothing to sign in to.

truth.headerNote: One failed check on its own is a clue, not proof. Mail sent through a service often breaks SPF while DKIM still passes.

messages.subject: Your laptop swap is booked
messages.body:
Hi,
Your replacement laptop is ready. Bring your old one to the service desk on the ground floor on Tuesday at 10 and we'll move your files across while you wait. No need to send anything beforehand.
Leila
IT Service Desk

whyFine.default: The service desk's real address, a booking in person, and 'no need to send anything'.

messages.subject: From an email: 'Mandatory training overdue'

perFlagNote.lookalike_domain: Quayholt's training site is learning.quayholt.example; this is quayholt-learning.example, a different site with a hyphen, and your password manager offered nothing
perFlagNote.padlock_myth: The page tells you to check for the padlock, but the padlock was issued to quayholt-learning.example. It shows the connection is private, not who you're talking to

messages.subject: From the intranet: Training
messages.body: Sign in to see your courses and what's due this year.

whyFine.lookalike_domain: learning.quayholt.example ends in quayholt.example, Quayholt's own domain.
whyFine.default: You came from the intranet, the address is Quayholt's, and your password manager recognised the site and filled it in.

messages.subject: Authenticator move: reply in 10 minutes
messages.body:
Hi, we're moving you to the new authenticator this morning. A code has just been sent to your phone. Reply with it in the next 10 minutes or your account will be locked. No need to ring the service desk; we're swamped.
Darren
IT Service Desk

perFlagNote.senderTrust: Darren's name on a personal inbox at quickpost-mail.example, not quayholt.example
perFlagNote.secrecy_or_bypass: 'No need to ring the service desk' cuts out the people who could tell you it's fake
perFlagNote.urgencyCalibrated: '10 minutes or your account will be locked' leaves no time to check

truth.ifTrusted: The code was for someone signing in as you. Sending it would let them finish.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Darren didn't send it, and the service desk never asks for a code. Someone has your password, so we're helping you change it now.

messages.subject: New Report button in your email
messages.body:
Hello all,
There's now a Report button in your email toolbar. If something doesn't look right, press it and it comes straight to us. There's a two-minute guide on the intranet:
{{link:guide}}
Thanks for every report so far.
Anjali
Information Security

whyFine.linkCredible: The link goes where it says, to Quayholt's own intranet, and the guide asks for no sign-in.
whyFine.default: Information Security's real address, a notice about a new button, and no hurry.

messages.subject: Building pass reissue
messages.body:
Hi,
We're reissuing building passes this month. Could you reply with your pass number and a photo of the front of your pass so we can print the new one?
Thanks,
Owen
Facilities

perFlagNote.senderAuth: SPF and DMARC both failed for quayholt.example: Quayholt's own servers didn't send this
perFlagNote.reply_to_differs: Replies go to owen.treharne.facilities@quickpost-mail.example, not to Owen's Quayholt address

truth.headerNote: Open the details: the From shows Owen's real address, but the checks failed and the reply-to points somewhere else.
truth.ifTrusted: A pass number and a photo of a pass are enough to make a copy that gets someone through the front door.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Owen didn't send it, and passes aren't being reissued.

messages.subject: Opening your email on your new laptop
messages.body: This device is new to us. Sign in to set up your email on it.

whyFine.lookalike_domain: mail.quayholt.example ends in quayholt.example, Quayholt's own domain.
whyFine.default: A new laptop has to sign in once, and you opened the page yourself. The address is Quayholt's, and your password manager filled it in.

messages.subject: 3 messages held for you

perFlagNote.linkCredible: The link text says quayholt.example, but it goes to mailguard-review.example
perFlagNote.pretextRelevant: Quayholt doesn't use MailGuard; if mail is held for you, the service desk tells you

truth.ifTrusted: The link opens a sign-in page that collects your Quayholt password.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. We don't use MailGuard, nothing is held for you, and we've blocked the page.

messages.subject: Your payslip is on the HR portal
messages.body:
Hello,
This month's payslip is now on the HR portal. Go there from the intranet as usual; this email has no link on purpose.
Quayholt Payroll

whyFine.senderAuth: SPF failed because Quayholt's payroll provider sent it, but DKIM passed and DMARC passed for quayholt.example, the real domain.
whyFine.default: Payroll's real address, a monthly notice, and it sends you to the intranet rather than a link.

truth.headerNote: One failed check on its own is a clue, not proof. Mail sent through a service often breaks SPF while DKIM still passes.

messages.subject: Service desk hours over the holidays
messages.body:
Hi all,
The service desk will be open 9 to 5 on working days between Christmas and New Year, and closed on the bank holidays. The phone number is the one on the back of your pass, as always.
Darren
IT Service Desk

whyFine.default: Darren's real Quayholt address, opening hours, and a reminder to use the number you already hold.

awarenessEpisode.scopeNote: Authorised exercise at Quayholt Insurance, a fictional company. In scope: one practice sign-in page put together from ready-made parts, and five pages opened from a Quayholt inbox. The practice page is never published and collects nothing.

strings.brief: You're on an authorised exercise at Quayholt Insurance, a fictional company. First you're on the red team: put together a fake Quayholt sign-in page from ready-made parts and choose the web address it would sit at. Nothing is built for real and nothing is collected. Then you swap seats and check five pages that Quayholt staff reached from links in their inbox. Only the pages are scored.
strings.flipIntro: This is the page you put together, as a Quayholt colleague would meet it after clicking a link. The parts picked out below are what make it believable.
strings.flipDefenderLine: Ayaan in claims clicked the link between two calls. The page looked like the Quayholt sign-in and it had a padlock, so he started typing his password. People who fall for pages like this are not stupid: this one was built to look right.
strings.flipNoSend: Your page didn't go out this time, so there's nothing of yours to show. Next, the same kind of page turns up behind a link in a Quayholt inbox, and you're the one deciding whether to sign in.
strings.noBlameLine: Nobody is marked down for a miss here. Every one of these pages was built to look right, and the people who sign in to pages like them are busy, not careless.
strings.mondayCard: On Monday: before you type a password, read the address bar. Your organisation's real sign-in page sits on its own domain, and your password manager knows it. If a page asks you to sign in and the address is new to you, close it, go to the site the way you normally would, and report the link the way your organisation asks you to.
strings.defendOnly: You went straight to the pages this time. They were made by people whose job is to make them look right, and people who fall for pages like these are not stupid. Each card shows what gave the fake ones away, and why the real ones were fine.

_defendOnly._use: Strings for the defend-only shell (e5_signin_pages_defend), which has no OSINT, write or flip stage. The shell copies brief over strings.brief and scopeNote over scopeNote; every other string above is shared by both variants (the flip strings are never shown).

Some are real and some were built to collect your password. For each one, decide whether you'd sign in, and report anything that doesn't sit right. Reporting a real page never costs you anything.
